question: In the case of Vihaan Kumar vs. State of Haryana, what constitutional violation led the Supreme Court to declare the arrest illegal? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Violation of Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty)
Violation of Article 14 (Right to Equality)
Violation of Article 19(1)(a) (Freedom of Speech)
Violation of Article 22(1) (Failure to inform grounds of arrest)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Violation of Article 22(1) (Failure to inform grounds of arrest)

Explanation:
In the case of Vihaan Kumar vs. State of Haryana, the Supreme Court declared the arrest illegal because the police failed to inform the arrested person of the grounds of arrest. Article 22(1) mandates that no person shall be detained in custody without being informed of the grounds of arrest. This is a fundamental right that ensures personal liberty. The court held that the police's failure to comply with this constitutional requirement rendered the arrest unconstitutional. The judgment emphasized that violation of Article 22(1) automatically makes the arrest invalid. This case reaffirms the importance of procedural safeguards in arrests under the Indian Constitution.

☛ Article 22(2) → Right to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours
☛ Vihaan Kumar case → Arrest declared illegal due to violation of Article 22(1)
☛ Article 21 → Right to life and personal liberty, but main violation here was Article 22(1)
☛ Failure to inform grounds → Constitutes infringement of constitutional right
question_hi: विहान कुमार बनाम हरियाणा राज्य के मामले में, किस संवैधानिक उल्लंघन के कारण सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने गिरफ्तारी को अवैध घोषित कर दिया? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 21 का उल्लंघन (जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार)
अनुच्छेद 14 का उल्लंघन (समानता का अधिकार)
अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) का उल्लंघन (वाक् स्वतंत्रता)
अनुच्छेद 22(1) का उल्लंघन (गिरफ्तारी के आधारों को सूचित करने में विफलता)
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 22(1) का उल्लंघन (गिरफ्तारी के आधारों को सूचित करने में विफलता)

Explanation:
विहान कुमार बनाम हरियाणा राज्य के मामले में, सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने गिरफ्तारी को अवैध घोषित किया क्योंकि पुलिस ने गिरफ्तारी के आधारों की सूचना नहीं दी थी। अनुच्छेद 22(1) के अनुसार, किसी भी व्यक्ति को गिरफ्तार करते समय उसे गिरफ्तारी के कारणों की जानकारी देना अनिवार्य है। यह अधिकार व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता की रक्षा के लिए आवश्यक है। इस मामले में पुलिस ने यह संवैधानिक दायित्व पूरा नहीं किया, जिससे गिरफ्तारी असंवैधानिक हो गई। न्यायालय ने यह भी कहा कि अनुच्छेद 22(1) का उल्लंघन स्वतः ही गिरफ्तारी को अवैध बना देता है।

question: Who is responsible for implementing the RTI Act in public departments? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Director General
District Magistrate
Central Vigilance Officer
Central Public Information Officer
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Central Public Information Officer

Explanation:
Under the RTI Act, 2005, each public authority appoints a Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) or State Public Information Officer at the state level. These officers are responsible for processing information requests from citizens and providing the requested information within the stipulated time limit. The CPIO must provide information within 30 days of receiving the application. If the information is incorrect or incomplete, the CPIO is held accountable. Thus, the responsibility for implementing the RTI Act in public departments lies directly with the CPIO, not the Director General, District Magistrate, or Central Vigilance Officer.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the RTI Act enacted? → 2005
☛ What is the time limit to provide information? → 30 days
☛ Who is the first appellate authority? → Officer senior to CPIO
☛ What is the application fee for RTI? → ₹10
☛ Who constitutes the Central Information Commission? → Central Government
question_hi: सार्वजनिक विभागों में RTI अधिनियम को लागू करने के लिए कौन उत्तरदायी है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: महानिदेशक
जिला मजिस्ट्रेट
केंद्रीय सतर्कता अधिकारी
केंद्रीय लोक सूचना अधिकारी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है केंद्रीय लोक सूचना अधिकारी

Explanation:
RTI अधिनियम, 2005 के अनुसार, प्रत्येक सार्वजनिक प्राधिकरण में केंद्रीय लोक सूचना अधिकारी (CPIO) या राज्य स्तर पर राज्य लोक सूचना अधिकारी नियुक्त किए जाते हैं। ये अधिकारी नागरिकों से प्राप्त सूचना आवेदनों पर कार्रवाई करने और निर्धारित समय सीमा में सूचना उपलब्ध कराने के लिए उत्तरदायी होते हैं। CPIO का कर्तव्य है कि वह आवेदन प्राप्त होने के 30 दिनों के भीतर सूचना प्रदान करे। यदि सूचना गलत या अधूरी दी जाती है, तो CPIO जिम्मेदार होता है। इस प्रकार, RTI को लागू करने की जिम्मेदारी सीधे CPIO की होती है, न कि महानिदेशक, जिला मजिस्ट्रेट या केंद्रीय सतर्कता अधिकारी की।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

question: Which of the following is true about the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: It reviews the decisions of tribunals
It grants pardons to criminals
It settles disputes between the Union and states
It deals with criminal appeals only
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It settles disputes between the Union and states

Explanation:
The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India, defined under Article 131, deals exclusively with disputes between the Union and states or between states. This jurisdiction is specific to federal disputes and does not include appellate matters. Other options are incorrect: reviewing tribunal decisions falls under appellate jurisdiction; granting pardons is the President's power (Article 72); and criminal appeals also come under appellate jurisdiction. Thus, the correct description of original jurisdiction is settling disputes involving the Union and states. This provision ensures the Supreme Court acts as the highest federal court, resolving conflicts in the Indian federal structure.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article providing original jurisdiction to Supreme Court → Article 131
☛ Disputes between Union and states are filed in → Supreme Court
☛ Disputes between states come under which article → Article 131
☛ Power to grant pardons is with → President (Article 72)
☛ Review of tribunals is part of which jurisdiction → Appellate jurisdiction
question_hi: भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के मूल अधिकार क्षेत्र के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा सत्य है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: यह न्यायाधिकरणों के निर्णयों की समीक्षा करता है
यह अपराधियों को क्षमादान देता है
यह संघ और राज्यों के बीच विवादों का निपटारा करता है
यह केवल आपराधिक अपीलों से संबंधित है
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है यह संघ और राज्यों के बीच विवादों का निपटारा करता है

Explanation:
भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का मूल अधिकार क्षेत्र अनुच्छेद 131 में परिभाषित है। इसके तहत न्यायालय संघ और राज्यों या राज्यों के बीच विवादों का निपटारा करता है। यह अधिकार क्षेत्र विशेष रूप से संघीय ढांचे से उत्पन्न विवादों पर लागू होता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं: न्यायाधिकरणों के निर्णयों की समीक्षा सर्वोच्च न्यायालय अपीलीय अधिकार क्षेत्र में करता है; क्षमादान राष्ट्रपति का अधिकार है (अनुच्छेद 72); आपराधिक अपीलें अपीलीय क्षेत्र में आती हैं। इस प्रकार, मूल अधिकार क्षेत्र का सही उदाहरण संघ और राज्यों के बीच विवाद है।

question: Which of these is a distinct feature of a statutory corporation in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: It is fully owned by private shareholders and receives no government funding.
It has no legal existence separate from the government.
It is established by an Act, has a separate legal identity, and can sue or be sued.
Its employees are considered government civil servants under the usual rules.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is established by an Act, has a separate legal identity, and can sue or be sued.

Explanation:
A statutory corporation in India is created by a special Act of Parliament or State Legislature. It has a separate legal identity distinct from the government, enabling it to own property, enter contracts, and sue or be sued in its own name. Its employees are not government civil servants but employees of the corporation. While the government may provide financial support, the corporation is not fully owned by private shareholders; it is owned by the government. The key features include autonomy in operations, public accountability, and financial independence. The separate legal entity and ability to litigate are fundamental characteristics, distinguishing it from government departments and public companies.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What establishes a statutory corporation? → An Act of Parliament or State Legislature.
☛ Does a statutory corporation have a separate legal identity? → Yes, it is distinct from the government.
☛ Are employees of statutory corporations government servants? → No, they are employees of the corporation.
☛ Can a statutory corporation be sued? → Yes, it can sue or be sued in its own name.
☛ Example of a statutory corporation in India? → Indian Railways, LIC, RBI.
question_hi: इनमें से कौन सी भारत में एक सांविधिक निगम की विशिष्ट विशेषता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: यह पूरी तरह से निजी शेयरधारकों के स्वामित्व में है और इसे कोई सरकारी धन प्राप्त नहीं होता है।
इसका सरकार से अलग कोई कानूनी अस्तित्व नहीं है।
यह एक अधिनियम द्वारा स्थापित है, इसकी एक अलग कानूनी पहचान है, और यह मुकदमा कर सकता है या इस पर मुकदमा किया जा सकता है।
इसके कर्मचारियों को सामान्य नियमों के तहत सरकारी सिविल सेवक माना जाता है।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है यह एक अधिनियम द्वारा स्थापित है, इसकी एक अलग कानूनी पहचान है, और यह मुकदमा कर सकता है या इस पर मुकदमा किया जा सकता है।

Explanation:
भारत में एक सांविधिक निगम (स्टैट्यूटरी कॉरपोरेशन) संसद या राज्य विधानमंडल के एक विशेष अधिनियम द्वारा स्थापित किया जाता है। इसकी एक अलग कानूनी पहचान होती है, जो इसे सरकार से पृथक बनाती है। यह अपने नाम पर संपत्ति रख सकता है, अनुबंध कर सकता है, और मुकदमा कर सकता है या उस पर मुकदमा चलाया जा सकता है। इसके कर्मचारी सरकारी सेवक नहीं होते, बल्कि निगम के कर्मचारी होते हैं। सरकार इसे वित्तीय सहायता दे सकती है, लेकिन इसका स्वामित्व सरकार के पास होता है, निजी शेयरधारकों के पास नहीं। इस प्रकार, एक अलग कानूनी अस्तित्व और मुकदमा करने की क्षमता इसकी प्रमुख विशेषताएं हैं।

question: Which Indian judgment laid down the concept of ‘Basic Structure’ of the Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Golaknath v. State of Punjab
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala

Explanation:
In the 1973 landmark judgment of Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, the Supreme of India propounded the 'Basic Structure' doctrine. It held that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its basic structure. This ruling overruled the Golaknath case (1967) which had stated that fundamental rights could not be amended. The basic structure includes: supremacy of the Constitution, democratic republic, federal character, separation of powers, and judicial review. The Minerva Mills case (1980) later reaffirmed this doctrine and restricted Parliament's amending power.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which case laid down the Basic Structure doctrine? → Kesavananda Bharati (1973)
☛ Which case overruled Golaknath? → Kesavananda Bharati
☛ What did Minerva Mills emphasize? → Protection of basic structure
☛ What is NOT part of basic structure? → Economic policies
☛ Maneka Gandhi case relates to which Article? → Article 21's expanded meaning
question_hi: किस भारतीय फैसले ने संविधान की ‘मूल संरचना’ की अवधारणा को प्रतिपादित किया? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: गोलकनाथ बनाम पंजाब राज्य
केशवानंद भारती बनाम केरल राज्य
मिनर्वा मिल्स बनाम भारत संघ
मेनका गांधी बनाम भारत संघ
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है केशवानंद भारती बनाम केरल राज्य

Explanation:
1973 में केशवानंद भारती बनाम केरल राज्य मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने 'मूल संरचना' सिद्धांत प्रतिपादित किया। इसने निर्धारित किया कि संसद संविधान में संशोधन कर सकती है, किंतु संविधान की मूल संरचना को नष्ट या परिवर्तित नहीं कर सकती। इस निर्णय ने गोलकनाथ मामले (1967) के फैसले को खारिज कर दिया, जिसमें कहा गया था कि संसद मौलिक अधिकारों में संशोधन नहीं कर सकती। मूल संरचना में शामिल हैं: संविधान की सर्वोच्चता, लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य, संघीय ढांचा, शक्तियों का पृथक्करण और न्यायिक समीक्षा। बाद में मिनर्वा मिल्स मामले (1980) ने इस सिद्धांत को मजबूत किया।

question: Who among the following is eligible to be appointed as the Chairperson of the Lokpal, as per the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: A retired Cabinet Secretary of India
A sitting judge of a High Court
A current Member of Parliament
A former Judge of the Supreme Court

question: Which Schedule of the Constitution deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas in states, other than the Northeast? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)

Fifth Schedule
Sixth Schedule
solution:

Explanation:
The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than the northeastern states. It empowers the Governor to make regulations for the peace and good governance of these areas and mandates the formation of a Tribal Advisory Council. question: The 105th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2021, is related to which of the following? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Creation of a National Judicial Commission
GST reforms
Powers of state governments to identify OBCs
Women's reservation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Powers of state governments to identify OBCs

Explanation:
The 105th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2021, empowers state governments to identify and list Other Backward Classes (OBCs). This amendment was enacted after a Supreme Court ruling that held that states do not have the power to create OBC lists. The act amended Articles 342A, 366, and 367 of the Constitution. Previously, the list of OBCs was prepared based on the advice of the National Commission for Backward Classes. Now, states can create their own lists. This amendment strengthens federalism by granting states the authority to identify OBCs according to local conditions. It ensures that states have the autonomy to include or exclude communities based on regional social and educational backwardness.

question: In a State government, a minister holds office: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: for a fixed five-year term
during the pleasure of the Governor
as long as they enjoy the confidence of the State Legislative Council
during the pleasure of the President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is during the pleasure of the Governor

Explanation:
According to Article 164 of the Indian Constitution, ministers in a state government hold office during the pleasure of the Governor. This means that a minister does not have a fixed five-year term; rather, they serve at the discretion of the Governor. Although the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly, the tenure of each minister is subject to the Governor's pleasure. The Governor can dismiss a minister at any time, even if the minister enjoys the confidence of the assembly. This provision parallels the central government, where ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. Thus, the correct answer is that a minister holds office during the pleasure of the Governor, not for a fixed term or based on confidence of the Legislative Council.

question: What does the Constitution of India stipulate regarding the composition of the Election Commission of India (ECI)? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: It is constitutionally fixed as a single-member body headed by the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) only.
It must always be a three-member body (one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners).
It must include one Election Commissioner from each major state to ensure federal balance
It may be single or multi-member; initially, there was only a Chief Election Commissioner until 1989.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It may be single or multi-member; initially, there was only a Chief Election Commissioner until 1989.

Explanation:
Article 324 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Election Commission of India (ECI). It does not specify whether the Commission will be single-member or multi-member; rather, it states that the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) shall be appointed by the President, and other Election Commissioners may also be appointed as needed. Initially, until 1989, the ECI consisted of only the CEC, making it a single-member body. In 1989, the government appointed two additional Election Commissioners, making it a three-member body. Thus, the Constitution does not fix the composition but allows flexibility; it may be single or multi-member. The CEC can be removed only through a process similar to that of a Supreme Court judge, while other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC.

question: Under Article 254(2) of the Indian Constitution, a State law repugnant to a Central law can prevail in the State only if: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: it is passed by a special majority in the State Legislature
It is published in the State Gazette after legislative approval
it is reserved for the President’s consideration and gets his assent
it is certified by the Governor as necessary for public welfare
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is it is reserved for the President's consideration and gets his assent

Explanation:
Under Article 254(2) of the Indian Constitution, if a State Legislature makes a law on a subject in the Concurrent List that is repugnant to a Central law, it can prevail in that State only if it is reserved for the President's consideration and receives the President's assent. This provision allows the State to deviate from the Central law, but the President's assent ensures that national interests are safeguarded. Once the President gives assent, the State law overrides the Central law in that State. However, Parliament can later make a law on the same subject to supersede the State law.

question: Under Article 5 of the Indian Constitution, which of the following is NOT required for a person to be considered a citizen at the commencement of the Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Holding an Indian passport
Having at least one parent born in India
Having domicile in the territory of India
Being born in India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Holding an Indian passport

Explanation:
Article 5 of the Indian Constitution specifies citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution (January 26, 1950). It requires either birth in India, at least one parent born in India, or ordinary residence in India for at least 5 years immediately before the commencement. Holding an Indian passport is not a requirement under Article 5; passports are issued after citizenship is acquired and do not determine citizenship. Article 5 only covers those who were citizens at the start of the Constitution, not later acquisition or registration. The other three options—birth in India, parentage, or domicile—are directly mentioned in Article 5.

question: Which Constitutional Amendment removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: 44th Amendment Act, 1978
42nd Amendment Act, 1976
52nd Amendment Act, 1985
73rd Amendment Act, 1992
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 44th Amendment Act, 1978

Explanation:
The 44th Amendment Act (1978) removed the Right to Property (Article 31) from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A. It was passed by the Morarji Desai government. Earlier, the 39th Amendment (1975) and 42nd Amendment (1976) had restricted property rights. The 44th Amendment eliminated it as a fundamental right to allow the state to acquire property by law, provided compensation is paid. This amendment came into effect on June 20, 1979. It also introduced Article 300A to ensure no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law.

question: Which Act ended the monopoly of the East India Company over trade with India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 3)

Charter Act of 1833
Charter Act of 1813
solution:

Explanation:
The Charter Act of 1813 is known for ending the monopoly of the East India Company over trade with India. This act gave the British Parliament more control over Indian affairs and aimed to bring transparency to the Company's administration.

question: What is the primary function of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of the Indian Parliament?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 3)

To recommend the Union Budget
To assist in the election of the Speaker
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To review CAG audit reports

Explanation:
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) is a key standing committee of the Indian Parliament, constituted in 1921. Its primary function is to examine the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG). The committee ensures that public funds are used legally, efficiently, and for the intended purposes. It identifies financial irregularities in ministries and departments and reports its findings to Parliament. The PAC consists of 22 members, with 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha. The chairman is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. The committee plays a vital role in ensuring financial accountability of the executive.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for the power of the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes under the Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 342
Article 343
Article 336
Article 340
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 342

Explanation:
Article 342 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes. Under this article, the President, after consultation with the Governor, may specify tribes or tribal communities as Scheduled Tribes in relation to a state or union territory. Article 341 provides a similar provision for Scheduled Castes. Article 343 deals with the official language, while Article 336 makes special provisions for the Anglo-Indian community, and Article 340 deals with the appointment of a commission to investigate the conditions of backward classes.

question: Which of the following states was NOT formed through the State Reorganisation Act of 1956? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Rajasthan State

Mysore State
Bombay State
